name: Multipart Form Upload
description: Posts files to an HTTP endpoint as multipart/form-data, one request per file, and records each response's status and body.
introductoryText:
Uploads files from the Omniscope server to a web endpoint that accepts multipart/form-data, the way an HTML form with a file field does.

**How to set it up**: enter the upload URL. Then either connect records with a field of file paths (one request per record) and choose that field, or, with nothing connected, choose a single file. Add headers, an Authorization value and extra form fields if the endpoint needs them.

**Output**: the input records (or the single file's path) with the HTTP status, the response body (first 8,000 characters) and an error message for each file. A failed upload is recorded, not stopped: check the Error field downstream.

options.name: upload_url
options.title: Upload URL
options.description: The endpoint to POST each file to, starting with http:// or https://.

options.name: file_path_column
options.title: File to upload (no input)
options.description: The file to upload when no input is connected. With an input, the File path field is used instead.

options.name: file_path_field
options.title: File path field
options.description: With an input connected: the field holding each record's file path on the server. One request per record.

options.name: form_field_name
options.title: Form field name
options.description: The name of the multipart field that carries the file. Most endpoints expect file.

options.name: extra_fields
options.title: Extra form fields
options.description: Optional fields sent with every file, one per line as name=value, for example folder=invoices.

options.name: headers
options.title: Headers
options.description: Optional HTTP headers, one per line as Name: value, for example Accept: application/json. Saved as plain text in the project: put a secret in Authorization instead.

options.name: authorization
options.title: Authorization
options.description: Optional value of the Authorization header, such as Bearer followed by a token. Kept as a password.

blockOutputs.label: Results
blockOutputs.tooltip: One record per file: the input fields (or File path), HTTP status, Response (the body, truncated) and Error (empty when the upload succeeded).
